THOUGHT: Infertility is defined as failure to conceive after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse; this couple has tried for 15 months so infertility evaluation is appropriate. Major reversible organic causes are unlikely given normal ovarian reserve/hormonal profile (FSH, LH, estradiol, progesterone, testosterone normal) and a normal pelvic ultrasound without structural abnormalities (no fibroids or cysts). There is no evidence of pelvic infection on exam (no discharge, normal-appearing external genitalia). Male-factor contribution is possible (husband reports occasional erectile dysfunction) but that is described as intermittent and there is no semen analysis provided; however the patient’s primary limiting symptom is difficulty with vaginal penetration.

During the pelvic exam the patient’s pelvic floor muscles involuntarily tightened and discomfort aborted the speculum exam; she reports pelvic floor muscle tension with attempted penetration. These findings fit the clinical pattern of a penetration disorder characterized by involuntary pelvic floor tightening and pain/anxiety around penetration. The DSM-5 diagnosis that encompasses persistent difficulty with vaginal penetration, marked pain or fear of pain, and involuntary vaginal muscle tightening is genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder (previously termed vaginismus when muscle spasm predominated). Other organic causes (infectious vaginitis, anatomic obstruction, dermatologic disease, active pelvic pathology) have been reasonably excluded by history, exam, and imaging. Her known psychiatric history (body dysmorphic disorder) may contribute to anxiety and avoidance around sexual activity, supporting a psychophysiologic etiology rather than a primary endocrine or structural cause.

DIAGNOSIS: Genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder (vaginismus subtype)
